presentation.asset: Stripe-hosted Checkout and Customer Portal surfaces, constrained provider profile
presentation.typography: Provider-safe sans fallback, with Homa wording and action hierarchy preserved where Stripe does not accept custom font assets

configurableFields.updatePath: Deploy the Homa checkout route and its server configuration. Keep every Stripe Payment Link inactive; configured legacy link URLs identify only the exact recurring Price ids used to create Checkout Sessions.
configurableFields.fallback: Reject an invalid or expired family intent, a closing family, missing configuration, any active Payment Link, or an inexact price mapping before requesting a Checkout Session.
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Homa checkout intents expire after five minutes. Checkout Session URLs are one-time provider destinations and are not persisted or cached by Homa.
configurableFields.rollback: Disable Homa checkout entry points or restore the prior safe server-checkout commit while every Stripe Payment Link remains inactive. Never roll back by reactivating a public Payment Link.

configurableFields.updatePath: Set the trusted Homa site origin in Vercel and deploy Homa. The server builds the success URL at /api/billing/confirm and the cancel URL at /app; Stripe Dashboard does not own either destination.
configurableFields.fallback: Never follow a returned destination outside checkout.stripe.com. Missing, unverifiable, or unauthenticated confirmation returns to /app without granting access.
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Homa does not cache checkout destinations, Checkout Session verification, or entitlement state.
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the previous trusted Homa origin and safe server route, keep Payment Links inactive, and verify both success and cancel paths in Stripe sandbox before production re-enable.

configurableFields.updatePath: Stripe Dashboard Billing customer portal configuration
configurableFields.fallback: Return the authenticated family to /app/settings when no Stripe customer exists or the provider call fails
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Portal sessions are one-time provider URLs and are not persisted or cached by Homa
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the prior Stripe portal configuration and keep the Homa route fallback active

configurableFields.updatePath: Stripe Dashboard Developers Webhooks endpoint and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in Vercel
configurableFields.fallback: Acknowledge unknown families safely, return 503 when the endpoint is intentionally dark, and let Stripe retry transient failures
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Webhook events are processed idempotently into the family billing mirror, never from a cached browser state
configurableFields.rollback: Disable the endpoint in Stripe, restore the prior secret, and reconcile the family mirror before re-enabling

configurableFields.updatePath: Deploy the Homa deletion protocol with exhaustive, exact-family Stripe reconciliation before family access can close.
configurableFields.fallback: Preserve family access when Stripe is unavailable or uncertain, a configured Payment Link is active, pagination is incomplete, tenant ownership conflicts, or a subscription does not reach a terminal provider state.
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Homa does not cache deletion-time Stripe reads. The durable deletion job records only the bounded reconciliation outcome needed for safe retry.
configurableFields.rollback: Keep account deletion unavailable until the prior code and provider state are reconciled, and keep every Stripe Payment Link inactive throughout rollback.

environment.notes: Test and live Stripe keys are selected server-side. Configured Payment Link URLs are server-only price lookup inputs and every matching Stripe Payment Link must remain inactive.

records.fallback: Checkout fails closed when the intent, family, configuration, link-inactivity, or exact-price checks fail, and an untrusted returned destination is never followed. Confirmation returns to /app and Portal errors return to settings.
records.cache: No checkout, portal, customer, or entitlement response is cached by Homa.
records.updatePath: Homa server checkout deployment and Vercel environment configuration, plus Stripe Prices, inactive Payment Link reference objects, Customer Portal, and webhook configuration.

rollback.restoreAction: Disable Homa checkout entry points or restore the previous safe server-checkout commit while keeping every Payment Link inactive, then verify sandbox checkout, cancellation, confirmation, and account-deletion reconciliation before production re-enable.
rollback.restoreTarget: Homa-owned checkout route, Stripe Checkout Sessions, inactive price-reference links, Customer Portal, webhook endpoint, and Homa billing mirror

contracts: The client receives only a five-minute Homa checkout intent bound to the authenticated family, tier, and billing period.
Every Payment Link in the Stripe account remains inactive; configured legacy URLs recover only an exact recurring Price id with quantity one.
Homa creates success and cancel URLs from its trusted configured origin and follows only checkout.stripe.com as the returned provider destination.
Checkout Sessions collect a card before the explicit seven-day trial and carry the family id in client_reference_id, session metadata, and subscription metadata.
Entitlements are written only after verified Checkout or webhook evidence and remain idempotent.

Before family access closes for deletion, Homa expires every open exact-family Checkout Session and confirms every verified family-owned Stripe subscription is terminal; provider uncertainty preserves access.
Stripe retries transient webhook failures while unknown families are acknowledged without cross-tenant writes.
Payment failures return a truthful recovery destination instead of a branded dead end.

presentation.asset: Supabase Auth email template and callback surfaces, constrained provider profile
presentation.typography: DM Sans interface fallback with EB Garamond reserved for Homa-owned display contexts; email clients receive provider-safe fallback stacks

configurableFields.updatePath: Supabase Dashboard Authentication Email Templates, then capture a real delivered message
configurableFields.fallback: A user can request another link or return to /forgot-password when the token is expired
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Supabase owns token issuance and delivery; Homa does not cache reset tokens or provider message bodies
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the previous Supabase template and resend a fresh recovery email

configurableFields.updatePath: Supabase Dashboard Authentication URL Configuration and Homa redirect route
configurableFields.fallback: Reject unsafe next paths and redirect failed exchanges to /signin?error=oauth or /forgot-password?error=expired
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: PKCE verifier and auth cookies remain provider/session scoped, never application cache
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the prior allow-list entry and callback commit, then test one email and one OAuth exchange

environment.notes: Local, preview, and production redirect origins must be explicitly allow-listed in Supabase. Production callback uses the forwarded host only after same-origin path validation.

records.fallback: Expired or failed authentication links return to the relevant Homa recovery screen with a truthful explanation.
records.cache: Auth tokens, PKCE verifiers, and reset links are never cached by Homa.
records.updatePath: Supabase Dashboard templates and URL configuration, plus the callback/template source files.

rollback.restoreAction: Restore the prior template and redirect configuration, then run a sandbox reset and OAuth exchange before production re-enable.
rollback.restoreTarget: Supabase email template, redirect allow-list, callback, and recovery routes

contracts: Session cookies are minted only by Supabase's verified code exchange.
next paths are same-origin and safe before they influence a redirect.
Expired recovery tokens never create a session and return to the recovery screen.
Tenant identity is derived from the authenticated Supabase session, never provider callback text.

presentation.asset: Google hosted consent screen and system browser session, constrained provider profile
presentation.typography: Google and system consent UI owns its provider typography; Homa owns the entry surface and uses DM Sans interface styling

configurableFields.updatePath: Supabase Google provider settings and redirect allow-list, paired with the Homa callback route
configurableFields.fallback: Return to Homa sign-in with an OAuth error and preserve a safe /app destination
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: OAuth code and PKCE verifier are single-use provider/session values, never cached by Homa
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the previous redirect allow-list and callback commit, then run one sign-in in sandbox

configurableFields.updatePath: Supabase redirect allow-list plus the Homa app scheme and shipped native binary
configurableFields.fallback: Dismissal or a missing code leaves the user on the native sign-in screen with a recoverable message
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: The system browser owns the OAuth session; Homa exchanges the one-time code and stores only Supabase's session
configurableFields.rollback: Restore homa://auth/callback and the previous app binary configuration, then verify a development build

environment.notes: Web uses /auth/callback. Native uses the exact homa://auth/callback deep link because the provider allow-list requires a stable literal URI.

records.fallback: Provider cancellation and callback errors return the user to Homa's sign-in surface without creating partial account state.
records.cache: No Google token, consent response, or authorization code is cached by Homa.
records.updatePath: Google provider configuration through Supabase, the Homa web callback, and native scheme configuration.

rollback.restoreAction: Restore the prior provider redirect configuration and native scheme, then verify one web and one native sign-in in sandbox.
rollback.restoreTarget: Google provider settings, Supabase redirect allow-list, Homa callback, and native deep link

contracts: OAuth returns through a safe same-origin path before Homa creates the session.
Native OAuth uses the system browser instead of an embedded WebView.
A missing or failed code never silently reports a signed-in state.
The authenticated Supabase session remains the only authority for family identity.

presentation.asset: Apple system Sign in with Apple sheet, constrained provider profile
presentation.typography: Apple system sheet owns provider typography; Homa owns the entry surface and uses DM Sans interface styling

configurableFields.updatePath: Apple Developer capability and Expo native entitlement, followed by a store-signed build
configurableFields.fallback: Dismissal or a missing identity token leaves the user on sign-in with a recoverable failure state
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Apple owns the account sheet; Homa forwards only the signed identity token to Supabase and does not cache it
configurableFields.rollback: Remove the entitlement only in a coordinated binary release and retain the alternate email path

environment.notes: Apple identity is currently a native system-sheet flow. The entitlement, bundle identifier, and Supabase Apple provider client configuration must agree.

records.fallback: Email sign-in remains available when Apple is unavailable, cancelled, or returns no identity token.
records.cache: No Apple identity token or private relay address is cached by Homa.
records.updatePath: Apple Developer capability, Expo app configuration, and Supabase Apple provider settings.

rollback.restoreAction: Keep email and Google sign-in visible, revert the native entitlement/configuration in the next binary, and verify the remaining identity paths.
rollback.restoreTarget: Apple entitlement, Supabase Apple provider client, and native sign-in entry

contracts: Apple's identity token is sent to Supabase's verified signInWithIdToken call.
A cancelled system sheet is not an authentication error and never creates a partial session.
Email and Google remain available as truthful alternatives.
Native identity is tied to the configured bundle identifier, not a client-supplied family ID.

presentation.asset: StoreKit purchase and restore UI plus Apple's subscription-management URL, constrained provider profile
presentation.typography: StoreKit and Apple's management surface own provider typography; Homa uses its native DM Sans and EB Garamond roles around the handoff

configurableFields.updatePath: App Store Connect subscription products plus Homa's broad receipt-recognition catalog and narrower new-purchase offer list.
configurableFields.fallback: If App Store products cannot load or a product is outside the current new-purchase list, keep purchase unavailable and do not guess entitlement.
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: StoreKit owns product availability. Homa persists a durable purchase journal on the device and a family-scoped server interlock until signed provider evidence resolves the attempt.
configurableFields.rollback: Keep App Store products unavailable, restore the previous product identifiers and catalog only if historical receipt recognition remains intact, then test restore before re-enabling purchases.

configurableFields.updatePath: Apply the purchase-interlock migration before deploying the interlock-aware server, then require an attempt-token-capable iOS build before StoreKit products can become available.
configurableFields.fallback: Keep App Store products unavailable. Any purchase that may have started retains its durable interlock, and unresolved provider state preserves family access and blocks deletion.
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: The mobile crash journal and server interlock survive process loss. Only signed Apple transaction evidence resolves a started attempt into durable billing truth.
configurableFields.rollback: Keep App Store products unavailable before reverting interlock-aware code. Never restore family-id purchase tokens or client cancellation of a purchase that may have started.

configurableFields.updatePath: Apple's documented subscription-management URL and native settings entry
configurableFields.fallback: Keep the Homa settings surface available if the external URL cannot open
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: The management URL is static and is not a customer-specific cached entitlement response
configurableFields.rollback: Restore the prior URL and settings copy, then open it from a signed store build

configurableFields.updatePath: App Store Connect App Store Server Notifications endpoint and Homa JWS verifier
configurableFields.fallback: A notification with no linked family is acknowledged without a cross-tenant write; unverifiable payloads fail closed
configurableFields.cacheBehavior: Apple notifications update the durable family subscription mirror; no notification is treated as browser cache
configurableFields.rollback: Disable the notification endpoint, restore the previous verifier and route commit, then reconcile affected family mirrors

environment.notes: The same webhook accepts signed sandbox and production notifications. App Store products remain unavailable until a minimum attempt-token-capable build is enforced, signed auto-renew state is persisted, immediate deletion UX is compliant, and StoreKit sandbox evidence passes.

records.fallback: A failed purchase or unavailable catalog keeps the paywall closed to entitlement claims, offers retry or restore, and leaves account access truthful.
records.cache: Entitlement truth comes from verified StoreKit transactions and the durable family mirror, never from a cached client flag.
records.updatePath: App Store Connect, StoreKit/native configuration, and the Homa Apple verification routes.

rollback.restoreAction: Keep App Store products unavailable, disable the changed Apple product or notification configuration, restore only interlock-safe verifier and catalog behavior, and verify restore and account access before reopening.
rollback.restoreTarget: StoreKit catalog, Apple subscription management handoff, App Store Server Notifications, and entitlement mirror

contracts: StoreKit transactions are verified server-side before entitlements change.

A fresh purchase uses a server-minted attempt id as appAccountToken, which must resolve to the exact authenticated family and signed product before access can change. Legacy family-id tokens are linked-history or restore evidence only, never fresh-claim safety.
The family-scoped purchase interlock commits before StoreKit opens. Once a purchase may have started, client cancellation cannot remove the deletion fence; signed Apple evidence must resolve it.
Apple subscription statuses normalize into the shared account-access vocabulary used by Stripe.
Provider outages never become a guessed paid state and never cross family boundaries.
App Store products stay unavailable until old builds cannot start a legacy-token purchase and the signed auto-renew plus immediate-deletion activation requirements are certified.
